findings.evidence: "Analyze the Requirements: Break down the user's idea into core components, data relationships, layout constraints..." and "Use consistent ASCII characters (|, -, +, =, *, #, etc.)"
findings.fix: Cut generic steps the model already follows. Keep only non-obvious knowledge, such as fixed-width alignment rules, box-drawing character choices that render safely, a standard width of 80 columns, and conventions for marking interactive states.

findings.evidence: "Provide: Detailed component breakdown, Suggested technology stack considerations, Implementation priority recommendations"
findings.fix: Delete or replace with concrete, project-specific handoff rules, such as naming the target framework the mockup maps to.

findings.evidence: No NEVER list or gotchas anywhere in the body.
findings.fix: Add specific anti-patterns with reasons. Never mix tab and space alignment, because columns break in proportional fonts. Never use Unicode box characters in mockups destined for plain-text docs. Never present variants that differ only cosmetically. Never begin implementation before the user picks a mockup.

findings.evidence: Five-step list: Analyze, Generate, Rationale, Selection, Transition.
findings.fix: Add thinking heuristics, for example how to pick axes of variation (density, navigation placement, information hierarchy) so that 3-5 variants really differ. Add a self-check of alignment and width before output.

findings.evidence: description: "Use this agent when you need to visualize UI concepts through ASCII mockups before implementation. Examples: <example>Context: ..." with long inline examples and commentary, and no boundaries
findings.fix: Use this agent when the user wants to sketch, wireframe or visualize a UI layout (dashboard, form, page, component, screen) as ASCII or text mockups before building it, and wants several layout options to choose from. Not for generating real HTML/CSS code, image mockups, or reviewing existing UIs.

findings.evidence: "Create 3-5 distinct ASCII mockup variations" with no default and "production-ready blueprints"
findings.fix: Set a default of 3 variants and say when to produce fewer (a simple form) or more. Drop the 'production-ready' claim, since ASCII is a sketch.

findings.evidence: "Always start by confirming your understanding of the requirements before generating mockups"
findings.fix: State what to do when requirements are vague or the user does not respond: ask at most 2-3 targeted questions, otherwise proceed with stated assumptions. Also cover user rejection of all options and very wide or complex layouts. Add a short ordered checklist or a sample mockup output template.

findings.evidence: No eval file found for this agent.
findings.fix: Add a small eval set with prompts (dashboard, contact form, an ambiguous request) and verifiable assertions, such as 3-5 variants, aligned borders, and a prompt asking the user to choose.
